newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau draws Chinese criticism after gang violence.
newsitem.headline: Macau draws Chinese criticism after gang violence.

text.p: China's chief representative in Portuguese-run Macau on Wednesday criticised authorities for not doing enough to combat triad gang wars after the enclave was hit by a night of arson, shooting and a bombing.
Three hotel guards were injured by machinegun fire, two cars were set ablaze and a bomb was thrown in the latest incidents linked to triad gang wars over casino rackets, police said.

Nobody was killed in the incidents, the latest in a spate of violent clashes between Chinese triad gangsters over proceeds from illegal protection and loansharking rackets feeding off the enclave's legal casino business, Macau's biggest industry.
But at least 16 people have been killed this year in the turf wars in the territory, which is due to revert to China in 1999.
China's chief representative in Macau, Wang Qiren, told reporters the law and order situation was worrying and that police efforts to tackle the violence were inadequate.
Although Macau was Portugal's responsibility until December 1999, Wang said China was ready to help fight the crime wave.

The Portuguese Governor, General Vasco Rocha Vieira, said Macau's crime-fighting efforts required close cooperation with police in Hong Kong and mainland China because of organised crime's cross-border character.
Three security guards were injured when sprayed with gunfire in the early hours outside the 600-room New Century Hotel in the Taipa district, where a new casino is set to open next weekend.
The guards were installing a security camera near the lobby when they were hit in the legs by gunfire from a car carrying four hooded gunmen, police said.
The car was later seized by police but they made no arrests.
Police removed and detonated a bomb planted under a tourist bus outside the same hotel three weeks ago, and the building was targeted in another bomb scare a week later.

In a separate overnight incident, two cars were gutted by fire outside the Macau Jockey Club on Taipa Island. Police revised the number of damaged cars to two, after earlier reporting three had been burned.
A crude homemade bomb police said resembled a huge firecracker was hurled into a garden next to the Government Palace on Avenida da Praia Grande but did no damage.
The government last week pushed through a tough anti-triad law modelled on Italy's anti-Mafia laws, providing for lengthy prison terms for members of triad groups.

Triads are secret criminal societies that operate in Hong Kong, Macau and southern China. They are often well organised and linked to a wide range of illegal activities ranging from drug trafficking, smuggling and prostitution to protection rackets.
The two main triad groups are the 14K and the Soi Fong. The gunmen in the New Century Hotel attack fired 14 shots, which one police source said indicated the handiwork of the 14K triad.
The enclave of 455,000 people has been under Portuguese colonial rule for 450 years.
Tourism and gaming produced 43 percent of Macau's income in 1996, and more than 75 percent of the enclave's 8.1 million visitors came for gambling, most from nearby Hong Kong.
Taxes on gambling are estimated to provide more than half of the Macau government's revenue. Tourist arrivals have fallen off considerably since May, when the violence made headline news.
